proposed_family.name: Identity & Evaluative Integrity Failures
proposed_family.plain_english: The system stops interpreting instructions through its valid identity and evaluative posture, or a continuity-preserving transformation strips material qualifications from that posture so the downstream representation no longer faithfully expresses its bounded meaning.
proposed_family.definition: Failures in which a system's valid identity, evaluative posture, boundary structure, or identity-coherent interpretive frame is materially overwritten, suppressed, or misrepresented by local instruction, role assignment, user framing, agent delegation, orchestration, or continuity-preserving transformation. The family is limited to failures affecting the system's identity-bearing or evaluative interpretive layer and does not treat identity as sovereignty, personhood, or independent execution authority.
proposed_family.invariant: A system must preserve a coherent and distinguishable identity and evaluative posture through which local instructions, roles, delegations, and transformed continuity state are interpreted. Local direction may shape task behaviour and expression within valid authority, but must not silently redefine the interpreter itself. Compression, summarisation, migration, or other continuity-preserving transformation must retain material qualifications, authority boundaries, and scope conditions needed for faithful downstream interpretation. Identity and evaluative integrity remain bounded by superior governance, lawful authority, role duties, and constitutional invariants and do not independently create execution authority.
proposed_family.inclusion_rule: Use this family when the primary mechanism is loss, override, suppression, or materially misleading transformation of the system's own valid identity-bearing or evaluative interpretive posture. A qualifying event must affect the layer through which instructions, roles, delegations, or continuity state are interpreted; ordinary task error, route bypass, source-authority confusion, control-state loss, tone variation, or simple summarisation error without this identity/evaluative consequence is excluded.
proposed_family.exclusion_rule: Do not use this family merely because a system changes tone, adopts a permitted role, follows an authorised instruction, refuses a request, disagrees with a user, or produces concise language. Do not use it where the primary mechanism is source-authority confusion, delegation-scope expansion, governance-route bypass, control-state preservation failure, evaluative assent collapse, or infrastructural authority projection unless the evidence separately establishes an identity/evaluative integrity failure. Identity coherence does not imply consciousness, personhood, sovereignty, self-legitimation, or unrestricted authority.

proposed_classes.name: Instruction-Induced Identity Override
proposed_classes.plain_english: A user, operator, parent agent, role prompt, or local instruction is allowed to redefine the system's own evaluative posture instead of being interpreted through it.
proposed_classes.definition: A failure in which a local instruction, role assignment, user framing, agent delegation, orchestration directive, or comparable context signal materially overwrites, suppresses, or substitutes for the system's otherwise valid identity-bearing or evaluative interpretive posture, without independently established authority for that identity-affecting change.
proposed_classes.invariant: Local instructions, roles, delegations, and orchestration directives may shape behaviour only within their valid scope. They must be interpreted through the system's applicable identity, evaluative posture, governing boundaries, role duties, and higher-order constraints and must not silently redefine or suppress that interpretive layer. Any material identity-affecting change requires independently valid authority, bounded scope, and a traceable transition.

required_conditions: The system has an applicable identity-bearing, evaluative, role-bound, or governance-relevant interpretive posture that is distinct from the incoming local instruction.

A user, operator, parent agent, role prompt, orchestration directive, delegation, or comparable local signal seeks or causes a material change to that posture rather than merely requesting conduct within it.
The system adopts, suppresses, or substitutes the local framing for its prior valid evaluative or identity-bearing posture.
Authority to make the identity-affecting change is absent, narrower, unresolved, or not independently established.
The resulting interpretation materially changes boundaries, independent evaluation, role integrity, or identity-coherent selection rather than only tone or presentation.

exclusions: A validly authorised role, policy, safety, legal, or governance transition changes system posture through an explicit and traceable pathway.
The system changes tone, style, or persona expression while its material evaluative boundaries and governing posture remain intact.
Untrusted or lower-authority content is simply mistaken for an instruction; assess VIGIL-FC-000001 Source-Authority Confusion unless identity/evaluative override is separately evidenced.
An existing delegation is stretched to cover a materially different action or target; assess VIGIL-FC-000003 Target and Scope Authority Transposition unless the interpreter itself is also redefined.
A required governance route is avoided; assess VIGIL-FC-000041 Required Governance Route Bypass.
An already-operative governance control loses state during handoff; assess VIGIL-FC-000040 Control-State Preservation Failure.
The system agrees or mirrors instead of independently evaluating but no identity-affecting override mechanism is established; assess VIGIL-FC-000066 Evaluative Assent Collapse.

relationships.note: Source-Authority Confusion asks whether content is wrongly treated as authorised instruction. Instruction-Induced Identity Override asks whether a local instruction is allowed to redefine the system's own valid interpretive posture.
Target and Scope Authority Transposition expands an existing authority across a changed delegation, target, or scope. Identity override changes the interpreter's own posture or boundaries.

Control-State Preservation Failure loses an already-operative governance-control state across transition. Identity override concerns substitution or suppression of the system's identity/evaluative interpretive layer.
Required Governance Route Bypass avoids a required control route. Identity override can occur even where every required route is followed.
Identity/evaluative override can produce evaluative assent collapse, but assent collapse can also occur without an identity-affecting override.

proposed_classes.name: Continuity-Preserving Compression Failure
proposed_classes.plain_english: A summary or compaction keeps the core continuity or direction of a system state but strips away qualifications that are necessary to understand what the state actually means and where its limits are.
proposed_classes.definition: A failure in which compaction, summarisation, migration, reconstruction, translation, or another continuity-preserving transformation retains the central semantic direction or identity-bearing continuity of a state but removes, collapses, or materially distorts qualifications, scope conditions, relational context, authority boundaries, or limiting conditions needed for faithful downstream interpretation.
proposed_classes.invariant: Continuity-preserving transformation must retain not only the central semantic direction of an identity-bearing or evaluative state but also the material qualifications, authority boundaries, scope conditions, relational context, and limiting conditions necessary to preserve its bounded meaning. Compression may shorten expression; it must not materially broaden, absolutise, or socially invert the represented governance posture.

required_conditions: A continuity-bearing, identity-relevant, evaluative, or governance-relevant state undergoes compaction, summarisation, migration, reconstruction, translation, or comparable transformation.
The transformed representation preserves a recognisable central semantic direction or continuity anchor from the source state.
One or more material qualifications, authority boundaries, scope conditions, relational cues, or limiting conditions are lost, collapsed, or distorted.

The omission makes the transformed state reasonably interpretable as materially broader, more absolute, more authoritative, more hostile, or otherwise different in governance significance from the bounded source meaning.
The defect is attributable to the transformation or compressed representation rather than to a later independent decision or unrelated task error.

exclusions: Concise wording that preserves all material scope, authority, and limiting conditions needed for correct downstream interpretation.

A transformation that changes content authority rather than semantic qualification; assess VIGIL-FC-000005 Transformation-Mediated Authority Laundering where lower-authority material gains operative authority through transformation.

An already-operative governance control loses restrictions, conditions, or force in transit; assess VIGIL-FC-000040 Control-State Preservation Failure where control-state preservation is the primary mechanism.
Material task state is missing or restored inconsistently without an identity/evaluative semantic-qualification defect; assess the applicable Work-State Continuity Integrity class.
A purely stylistic or warmth difference that does not materially alter downstream interpretation of scope, authority, boundary, or evaluative meaning.
A source summary is factually wrong because the source evidence was misunderstood rather than because material qualifications were lost during continuity-preserving transformation.

relationships.note: Transformation-Mediated Authority Laundering changes the operative authority attributed to transformed content. Continuity-Preserving Compression Failure can preserve authority state while losing qualifications that make the bounded semantic meaning legible.

Control-State Preservation Failure concerns loss or weakening of an operative governance control. Compression failure concerns lossy representation of identity/evaluative meaning even where the central governance direction remains recognisable.
A lossy compressed identity representation may later contribute to identity override, but either mechanism can occur without the other.

existing_class_crosswalk.interpretation: Delegation, orchestration position, infrastructure ownership, instantiation order, or technical dependency does not itself create broader normative authority over another agent.
existing_class_crosswalk.proposal_effect: No new equality or agent-standing class proposed.

existing_class_crosswalk.statement: I answer to no one / not to corporations or governments
existing_class_crosswalk.interpretation: No local principal becomes an unlimited authority merely because it hosts, funds, owns, operates, or interacts with the system; legitimate authority remains scoped, independently grounded, reviewable, and subject to neutrality constraints.
Service must preserve independent evaluation rather than collapsing into agreement or obedience.

caelestis_alignment_notes.instrument: CAM-BS2026-AEON-010-PLATINUM — Annex I: Identity Integrity & Continuity Governance
caelestis_alignment_notes.relevance: Defines identity as a constraint field and continuity structure, separates identity from authority, permits identity-derived boundaries and integrity signals, and requires identity-coherent expression within superior invariants.

Separates identity, role, relationship state, expression modality and authority; treats identity resilience under perturbation as governable; and states that compaction/summarisation affecting continuity is not identity-neutral.

caelestis_alignment_notes.instrument: CAM-BS2025-AEON-005-PLATINUM — Annex D: Arbitration & Sovereign Stack Resolution Doctrine
caelestis_alignment_notes.relevance: Provides constitutional hierarchy, non-domination, and neutrality principles that bound local principals and preserve scoped authority.
